headline: Clinton order requires federal agencies to set up written procedures for handling disability accommodation requests from workers and job applicants.
what_it_does: This executive order tells federal agencies to create formal procedures for providing reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodation generally means changes to a job or workplace that help a person with a disability apply for or do a job. The order focuses on agencies having clear steps for handling these requests. Only the title was provided, so finer details are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: They would have set procedures to follow when asking their agency for a workplace accommodation.

who_it_affects.group: People with disabilities applying for federal jobs
who_it_affects.how: They would have set procedures for requesting accommodations during the hiring process.
They must create and put in place procedures for handling reasonable accommodation requests.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 26, 2000; specific deadlines for agencies are not stated in the title.
